text: Compare and contrast the defences of volenti non fit injuria (voluntary assumption of risk) and
contributory negligence. [25]
Describe the elements of battery, in relation to the tort of trespass to the person. Assess the extent
to which hostility is a necessary element of battery. [25]
Describe the duty owed to a visitor under the Occupiers’ Liability Act 1957. Assess the extent to
which an occupier can avoid liability through the use of warnings and exclusion clauses. [25]
Section B
John, a 14 year old boy, is a member of a football club. During a training session he is seriously
injured when the goal post falls and hits him. The club’s management had previously been made
aware that the goal post was unstable but had not taken any action.
John’s parents, Ian and Margaret, receive a telephone call informing them that their son is seriously
injured and that an ambulance has been called. Ian and Margaret arrive at the football club just
as the ambulance is leaving. They follow the ambulance to the hospital. Margaret briefly sees
John, clearly badly injured, as he is taken out of the ambulance. John undergoes an emergency
operation and is unconscious for five days. Ian and Margaret sit at his bedside for the whole time.
John regains consciousness but spends a year in recovery.
Ian and Margaret have both been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to negligence. [25]
Several years ago Pablo purchased a luxury apartment on the tenth floor of a building in the city
centre, next to an art gallery. His apartment has floor to ceiling windows. He has never used any
form of window covering as it was not necessary due to the location of the apartment.
The gallery has recently added a viewing platform on the top floor so that visitors can experience
the views over the city. The viewing platform is also available for hire and is used in the evenings
for social events.
Pablo is concerned that the visitors on the viewing platform can now see into his apartment. He is
also finding the social events disruptive as they happen several nights a week with large numbers
of guests. These events often continue after midnight with loud music and sometimes flashing
lights. Pablo complains but the gallery management tells him that the viewing platform and events
are essential to its finances and continued existence.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in relation to private nuisance.
Ezra works as a junior programmer for a software development company, AB Ltd (AB). He applies
for a senior role with another company, DC Ltd (DC). DC contacts AB for an employment reference
for Ezra to indicate his suitability for the role. His manager, Susan, has only worked for AB for a
short time. She writes a very positive reference for Ezra. She does not check his work records
and therefore is not aware that he has a poor attendance record and has been given a number of
warnings about the quality of his work, by a previous manager.
Ezra starts work for DC. He is given responsibility for a valuable project, to provide a new software
package for a hospital. Due to his poor attendance at work and errors in the software, the project
is not completed on time and DC loses £1 million as a result.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in relation to negligent
misstatement. [25]
